saw.short: GTA VI's launch week: 420 million hours watched on streaming
saw.headline: *GTA VI’s launch week*: 420 million hours watched on streaming
saw.what: Streams Charts says GTA VI’s launch week drew 420 million hours watched, nearly triple the previous launch-week record, with a 7.91 million peak of concurrent viewers, per Dexerto. That is third-party data. Take-Two’s investor page lists a 20 Nov release headlined “$3.79 Billion in Day One Retail Sales”, but we couldn’t load its text. Earlier estimates from Sensor Tower were lower, so the figures don’t match.
saw.why: A launch that carried on for a week. Sales figures vary a lot between sources.

saw.short: Ofcom has had 887 complaints about the I'm A Celebrity camp row
saw.headline: *Ofcom* has had 887 complaints about the I’m A Celebrity camp row
saw.what: Ofcom says it received 887 complaints about Sunday’s I’m A Celebrity episode, in which Mariella Frostrup and AJ Odudu clashed, and “is yet to decide whether or not to investigate”, per Radio Times. Metro reports Ant and Dec say it “became a much bigger deal than it should have”. This is a sensitive story, so we have kept to the facts.
saw.why: The biggest TV talking point of the week, and still running. Tone matters.

saw.short: Disney's Hexed opens in UK cinemas today
saw.headline: Disney’s *Hexed* opens in UK cinemas today
saw.what: Hexed opens in UK cinemas today. TheWrap’s pre-release projection, published 24 Nov, has a $40–45 million five-day US opening, likely second behind The Hunger Games, with a 65% Rotten Tomatoes score at the time. These are projections, not results. We haven’t seen a UK reviews round-up beyond the Radio Times review.
saw.why: Our client’s release day. The projection is a guide, not a result.

saw.short: Radio 1's Big Weekend 2027 is heading to Brighton
saw.headline: *Radio 1’s Big Weekend 2027* is heading to Brighton
saw.what: Greg James revealed on air on Thursday that Radio 1’s Big Weekend 2027 will be at Preston Park, Brighton, from Friday 28 to Sunday 30 May, per BBC News and NME. He said: “If Radio 1 was a place, it would be Brighton.” BBC says about 70 acts, and NME puts capacity at 80,000, so we have used BBC’s wording.
saw.why: A festival announcement that gets a local and national response. Start planning early.

saw.short: A baby hippo is born at Longleat
saw.headline: A *baby hippo* is born at Longleat
saw.what: Metro reports a hippo calf was born last week to mother Matylda at Longleat in Wiltshire, as part of the European breeding programme. Its sex isn’t yet known. Longleat’s Darren Beasley said keepers are “over the moon”. Metro’s headline says it is the first in 40 years, which we haven’t seen supported in the text.
saw.why: A feel-good animal story that travels well. The ‘first in 40 years’ line is unconfirmed.

saw.short: Bournemouth win their first five European games
saw.headline: *Bournemouth* win their first five European games
saw.what: Bournemouth won away at Celta Vigo in the Europa League on Thursday after going 1-0 down and having Bafode Diakite sent off, per BBC Sport. Álvaro Rodríguez and Rayan scored in the second half, for a club-record 10th straight win in all competitions. BBC says they are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches.
saw.why: A big football story outside the Big Six. Fans will make it a talking point.

platform.short: X launches its first parental controls for teens
platform.headline: *X* launches its first parental controls for teens
platform.what: X’s new controls for 13 to 17 year olds let parents see time spent, set daily limits, require approval for new followers and limit For You to accounts the teen follows, per The Verge and Engadget. A parent can link up to five teens, both sides must agree, and parents can’t read DMs or searches. Teen accounts default to protected mode.
platform.why: A teen-safety first for X. Relevant for family-facing brands.

platform.headline: *WhatsApp* adds scheduled messages
platform.what: WhatsApp says users can schedule a message from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead, in one-to-one and group chats, for text, photos and videos. It stays end-to-end encrypted and delivers even if the phone is off. It is rolling out globally “over the coming weeks”, per the WhatsApp blog.
platform.why: Handy for community managers and campaigns. Rollout is gradual.
